LANDING WAVE. Merged this session: de95 flake fix (2072 - removes the recurring spurious Verified -1), 4cee (2075), 25b4 (2080), 7e0d (2078), plus the earlier 6f18/1cf6/4329/111a/7931. In review: 2074 fcb7, 2076 dff2, 2077 a4d7, 2079 1dd5 (re-pushed), 2082 111a-guard, 2083 4329-guard, 2084 44ff, 2085 d6e3.

MISSING GUARDS FOUND AND BUILT. The close-out investigation found 4329 and 111a shipped their consolidation but NOT the construct-uniqueness guard their own AC1 names - the epic's whole thesis. Audited the other two children: 6f18 and 7931 both have real scanning guards (6f18 via _tracker_sibling_offenders + the store-path-ok marker rule; 7931 via an AST rglob over src/rebar). Proved 7931's has teeth by appending a second 'def _shadow' to _store/hlc.py and watching test_each_helper_is_defined_exactly_once fail with both paths named. Authored the two missing guards as 2082 (111a: conjunction of 'find_inbound_relationships(' and '"supersedes"', mutation-proven three ways - unmarked copy fails, reasoned marker excuses, BARE marker still fails) and 2083 (4329: parametrised over the LIVE table).

SELF-CAUGHT TAUTOLOGY: my first 4329 test parametrised over the table but drove the INJECTED walk, which is table-agnostic and passes for any row by construction - it looked like coverage and proved nothing. Rewrote it to go through the real rebar.transition; mutating transition to ignore the (closed, open) row now fails exactly that case. Kept the unit-tier test with a docstring stating plainly it cannot prove wiring. Also recorded that 4329's AC2 is not literally satisfiable: claim only ever walks open -> in_progress.

2079 BLOCKING FINDING WAS REAL AND IS FIXED. The reviewer found the gate evaluated the repeat-fix window at wall-clock now while the backtest passed the commit's timestamp - so replaying a historical commit scored it against TODAY's history, and the backtest reported that as the gate's recall. Two implementations of one rule disagreeing silently: the exact defect class this epic exists to end. Threaded base_ref/at through escalation_for_diff and rewired the backtest to call the GATE instead of the predicate beneath it. New test drives the same repo through two anchors and gets two verdicts; reverting the forwarding to at=None kills it.
